previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and a history of orthostatic hypotension was admitted for evaluation of hypotension and chest pain. He presented from cardiology clinic with systolic blood pressure as low as 85, presyncope, and self-resolving chest pressure. Initial workup ruled out acute myocardial infarction, with normal cardiac enzymes and EKGs showing only minimal changes. He was found to have acute kidney injury with creatinine rising from baseline 1.2 to 1.5, attributed to chronic dehydration from his mitochondrial disorder. He received IV fluids, which improved renal function to creatinine 1.1. His blood pressure medications—clonidine, diltiazem, and isosorbide mononitrate—were held due to symptomatic orthostasis and bradycardia. Metoprolol was reduced to 25 mg daily. Valsartan was continued. He was discharged home with plans to follow up for autonomic dysfunction and GI evaluation for malabsorption, with instructions to restart isosorbide mononitrate in clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
Pt is a ___ man with history of coronary artery disease, 
hypertension, dyslipidemia presenting symptoms of dehydration 
(higher UOsm, Cr), autonomic dysfunction in setting of 
medication changes, and associated chest pain. The pt was found 
to be dehydrated. Agressive rehydration was initiated and 
symptoms improved with fluids. There was a question of the cause 
of dehydration potentially being related to malabsorption 
problem but this was felt to be best evaluated by GI in the 
outpt setting. Because the pt felt he had adverse reaction to 
imdur despite lowered dose of 15mg Imdur was d/c'd but 
Metoprolol Succinate 25 mg BID home dose was continued 
w/reasonably good BP control. Pt was discharge in stable good 
condition w/instructions to drink plenty of fluids and with 
outpt follow-up for further evaluation and management.
.
Pt was full code during this admission

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with lightheadedness, mild 
non-radiating chest pain and excessive sweating. Tests were 
performed to rule out a possible heart attack; all of these 
heart related tests were negative for signs of heart attack. It 
was determined from blood and urine tests that you were 
dehydrated at which point you were given IV fluids. Your 
symptoms resolved with IV fluids. Given your ongoing 
difficulties with remaining hydrated at home as a results of 
absorption issues, we recommend follow-up with your 
gastroenterologist as soon as possible.

The following changes were made you your medications:
- Please STOP taking Isosorbide Mononitrate [Imdur]
- Please STOP taking Nexium and SWITH to Famotidine (Oral) 20 mg 
Tablet twice a day
- Please CONTINUE taking Metoprolol Succinate XL 25 mg twice per 
day
- Please continue to take all of your other home medications as 
prescribed.
.
Please be sure to take all medication as prescribed.
.
Please be sure to take extra care to ensure that you are 
hydrated to prevent this in the future. Given your malabsorption 
problems, you should drink as much as possible including water 
and beverages w/electrolytes (e.g., juice, gatorade, etc.).
.
Please be sure to keep all follow-up appointments with your PCP 
and gastroenterologist.
.
It was a please taking care of you and we wish you a speedy 
recovery.
